subtopic: Property of an Angle Bisector of a Triangle
stem:
In \(\triangle PQR\) seg PM is a median. Angle bisectors of \(\angle PMQ\) and \(\angle PMR\) intersect side PQ and side PR in points X and Y respectively. Prove that XY \(\parallel\) QR.

Complete the proof by filling in the boxes.

In \(\triangle PMQ\), ray MX is bisector of \(\angle PMQ\).

\(\therefore \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}} = \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}}\) .......... (I) theorem of angle bisector.

In \(\triangle PMR\), ray MY is bisector of \(\angle PMR\).

\(\therefore \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}} = \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}}\) .......... (II) theorem of angle bisector.

But \(\frac{MP}{MQ} = \frac{MP}{MR}\) .......... M is the midpoint QR, hence MQ = MR.

\(\therefore \frac{PX}{XQ} = \frac{PY}{YR}\)

\(\therefore\) XY \(\parallel\) QR .......... converse of basic proportionality theorem.

In \(\square\) ABCD, seg AD \(\parallel\) seg BC. Diagonal AC and diagonal BD intersect each other in point P. Then show that \(\frac{AP}{PD} = \frac{PC}{BP}\)

In fig 1.80, XY \(\parallel\) seg AC. If 2AX = 3BX and XY = 9. Complete the activity to find the value of AC.

Activity : 2AX = 3BX \(\therefore \frac{AX}{BX} = \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}}\)

\(\frac{AX + BX}{BX} = \frac{\text{(blank)} + \text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}}\) .......... by componendo.

\(\frac{AB}{BX} = \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}}\) .......... (I)

\(\triangle BCA \sim \triangle BYX\) .......... (blank) test of similarity.

\(\therefore \frac{BA}{BX} = \frac{AC}{XY}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles.

\(\therefore \frac{\text{(blank)}}{\text{(blank)}} = \frac{AC}{9}\) \(\therefore\) AC = (blank) ...from (I)

(In Fig. 1.80, X lies on side AB and Y on side BC of \(\triangle ABC\).)
note: In Fig. 1.80, X lies on side AB and Y on side BC of \(\triangle ABC\). The printed ANSWERS section gives the third blank as 5/3 and AC = 15, which contradicts its own preceding entry (3+2)/2 = 5/2; see the solution.
